boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named, documented destinations on nearby downtown Ashland corridors, each with one specific reason to stop.

cards.title: Ashland Theatre
cards.subtitle: England Street corridor — 205 England Street
cards.notes: Check the theatre calendar, then choose a first-run film, classic screening, or live performance that fits your visit.
cards.short_summary: Historic downtown venue for films and live entertainment.
cards.evidence_claim: Ashland Theatre is a historic film and performing-arts venue at 205 England Street offering first-run and classic films plus live music.
cards.access_notes: Ticket requirements vary by program; consult the theatre calendar before visiting.

cards.title: Sugar Fix Bakery
cards.subtitle: England Street corridor — 105-B England Street
cards.notes: Use the bakery as a quick England Street stop when you want to see its custom-decorated sugar cookies and baked goods.
cards.short_summary: Downtown bakery documented for decorated cookies and baked goods.
cards.evidence_claim: Sugar Fix Bakery at 105-B England Street offers custom-decorated sugar cookies and baked goods.
cards.access_notes: Purchases are required for bakery items.

cards.title: sweetFrog Ashland
cards.subtitle: England Street corridor — 210 England Street
cards.notes: Stop in for a build-your-own frozen-yogurt, gelato, sorbet, or topping combination while exploring downtown Ashland.
cards.short_summary: Frozen-dessert stop with a customizable format.
cards.evidence_claim: sweetFrog at 210 England Street offers frozen yogurt, gelato, sorbets, frozen drinks, and toppings.
cards.access_notes: Purchases are required for food and drink.

cards.title: Artistic Fusion Hair Company Mural
cards.subtitle: England Street corridor — 109 England Street
cards.notes: Walk past the salon’s steam-punk train mural and photograph it from the England Street sidewalk without entering the business.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor train-inspired mural on an England Street salon.
cards.evidence_claim: Artistic Fusion Hair Company at 109 England Street commissioned a steam-punk-inspired train mural completed in January 2023.
cards.source_title: Business Spotlight: Artistic Fusion Hair Company — Town of Ashland
cards.access_notes: Viewable from the public sidewalk; salon services require purchase or booking.

cards.title: Ashland/Hanover Visitor Center
cards.subtitle: North Railroad Avenue corridor — 112 N. Railroad Avenue
cards.notes: Pick up local maps and visitor information inside the 1920s train depot before continuing along the railroad corridor.
cards.short_summary: Visitor-information stop inside Ashland’s historic train depot.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ashland/Hanover Visitor Center occupies a 1920s train depot at 112 North Railroad Avenue and provides brochures, guides, and local information.
cards.source_title: Ashland/Hanover Visitor Center — Visit Ashland VA
cards.access_notes: The source lists varying daily hours; confirm before making a dedicated trip.

cards.title: Ashland Branch Library
cards.subtitle: South Railroad Avenue corridor — 201 S. Railroad Avenue
cards.notes: Browse a book, ask library staff for help, or use the branch as a quiet stop beside the tracks in downtown Ashland.
cards.short_summary: Public-library branch beside the downtown railroad corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Pamunkey Regional Library’s Ashland Branch is located at 201 South Railroad Avenue in downtown Ashland along the railroad tracks.
cards.access_notes: Library access and services follow Pamunkey Regional Library policies and hours.

cards.title: America’s Longest Railroad Mural
cards.subtitle: South Railroad Avenue corridor — 108 S. Railroad Avenue
cards.notes: Pause on South Railroad Avenue to view Ed Trask’s locomotive mural, which depicts a train that traveled Ashland’s tracks.
cards.short_summary: Large outdoor railroad-themed work by artist Ed Trask.
cards.evidence_claim: America’s Longest Railroad Mural at 108 South Railroad Avenue depicts a locomotive that traveled Ashland’s tracks 50 years earlier and was made by Ed Trask.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor viewing from the public corridor; respect adjacent property and traffic.

cards.title: Tiny Tim’s Trains & Toys
cards.subtitle: South Railroad Avenue corridor — 104 S. Railroad Avenue
cards.notes: Browse the train-and-toy shop while you are on the railroad corridor; it is a named downtown stop with a street address.
cards.short_summary: Named toy and train shop on the railroad corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Tiny Tim’s Trains & Toys is listed at 104 South Railroad Avenue in Ashland.
cards.source_title: July Events in Downtown Ashland, Virginia
cards.access_notes: Store merchandise requires purchase; verify shop hours directly before visiting.

cards.title: Ashland Museum & the Red Caboose
cards.subtitle: Hanover Avenue corridor — 105 Hanover Avenue
cards.notes: Arrange a museum or caboose visit to explore town history through objects, images, voices, and the restored 1926 railcar.
cards.short_summary: Local-history museum with a restored 1926 C&O caboose.
cards.evidence_claim: Ashland Museum at 105 Hanover Avenue interprets town history and offers tours of a fully restored 1926 C&O red caboose.
cards.access_notes: Groups are asked to call ahead to arrange a caboose visit.

cards.title: Hanover Arts & Activities Center
cards.subtitle: South Center Street corridor — 500 S. Center Street
cards.notes: Look for the center’s current arts or educational programming and take in the preserved building that began as an 1859 Baptist church.
cards.short_summary: Historic community center for arts, education, and activities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hanover Arts & Activities Center at 500 South Center Street occupies a building constructed in 1859 as a Baptist church and now hosts arts and educational activities.
cards.access_notes: Programs and entry requirements vary; check the center’s current schedule.
